data.body:
Final rebar-debug report

Problem: the bridge-preview-under-contention interface oracle could not acquire the reconciler lock because a standalone-loaded engine module attempted to import a top-level package that is intentionally absent.

Proven root cause: commit d9e0f0e733 introduced unconditional `from rebar_reconciler import git_adapter` imports at `_advisory_lock.py:83` and `_ref_lock.py:194`. Both modules execute by file path without package context under supported test/library paths, so the first import raised `ModuleNotFoundError`; bypassing it exposed the same failure in the nested ref-lock seam.

Proof: post-mortem runtime state showed an empty `__package__`, no `rebar_reconciler` in `sys.modules`, and `find_spec` returning None. Bypassing only `_lock_remote` reached and failed at `_ref_lock._git`. Seeding the supported package made the exact scenario pass. A fresh wheel proved ordinary top-level import is intentionally absent while `engine_env` and `_engine_module` work. The pre-d9 parent acquired/released a real ref lock in the same standalone context, pinning the regression to the refactor.

Test: the pre-existing interface oracle was collected/executed RED before repair at the exact first import. It was removed from the blind fixer filesystem, then restored GREEN. A hidden package-context collateral test proves both repaired seams reuse the canonical module object and observe module-qualified patches. Defect-seeded mutation of `_advisory_lock` returned the interface oracle to RED at that import; restoration returned GREEN. Independent mutation of `_ref_lock` returned it to RED at the nested import; restoration returned GREEN. The oracle asserts observable CLI JSON and preserved lock state, not internal source shape.

Fix: both seams now call exactly `lazy_load("rebar_reconciler.git_adapter", "git_adapter.py")`. The dotted key converges with unchanged package importers on one `sys.modules` object, restoring standalone execution without changing packaging, adapter behavior, or lock semantics.

Scope and safety: bounded caller sweep found no caller depending on the import failure; callers depend only on adapter behavior, which is unchanged. The fix restores pre-d9 behavior, adds no external dependency, creates no capability, and weakens no test. Package-context patch visibility is explicitly preserved.

Siblings: construct sweep checked every remaining `from rebar_reconciler import git_adapter` site. Two additional live standalone-loader failures were proven and filed/linked: `silt-resistant-gonolek` (`_concurrency.snapshot_head`) and `cinderlike-faulty-yucker` (`reconcile_helpers._commit_binding_store_snapshot`). `apply_outbound.py` and `__main__.py` are package-context-only and are not siblings. Parity census: CLI, MCP/API, library facade, automated reconciler, and lock read/write paths all converge on the repaired advisory/ref-lock core; no MISSING parity slot remains for this lock operation.

Residual risk and prevention: the two confirmed out-of-scope import fragilities are dispositioned by the linked tickets above. Unit-suite package seeding previously masked this class; fixed in scope by retaining the real standalone interface oracle and adding the canonical-module patch-visibility test. No other observed fragility is undispositioned.

Replication and gates: exact original reproduction passes; lock family 78 passed; full store suite 433 passed, 9 skipped; `make lint` passed; `make typecheck` passed; full `make test` passed with 13,819 passed, 60 skipped, 291 deselected. Commit `e481e5f3b175d8daabb5d9b6a4aef99f1e264825`, Change-Id `I6a9efa3760b186736544bda8b508bf55830b4e04`, ticket trailer and DCO verified. Not pushed or closed; serialized Gerrit/CI queue owns landing.
